clue.text: Annual visitor's journey round one capital!

indicators.note: the visitor and the journey are placed round the numeral, wrapping it

parts.note: Santa Claus visits once a year, at Christmas
the Roman numeral for one is I
to go is to journey

explanation.surface: Father Christmas makes his yearly trip around a single city.
explanation.walkthrough: Santa Claus is the annual visitor, arriving each Christmas; the exclamation mark points to a capital city as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

clue.text: Following fire, save old instrument

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job
save meaning except is but, as in 'all but one'

explanation.surface: After being dismissed, someone puts by an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is a Renaissance form of the trombone.

clue.text: Down, having cut back of neck

indicators.note: the last letter of the neck's synonym is removed

parts.note: the nape is the back of the neck

explanation.surface: Depressed after a haircut at the nape.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is soft fluff, and nap is the raised fuzzy surface of fabric.

clue.text: How reactors may be occupied, reproducing relatively closely?

definitions.meaning: breeder reactors produce more fissile material than they use, so such a reactor is busy at breeding

explanation.surface: Nuclear plants and family trees both multiplying close to home.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbreeding is mating between closely related individuals.

clue.text: Soldiers leave in great numbers at end of camp dance

indicators.note: the soldiers depart from the word for plenty, so their letters drop out

parts.note: galore means in abundance
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

indicators.note: the last letter of camp is taken

explanation.surface: Troops depart en masse after the camp's closing dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The galop is a lively 19th-century ballroom dance in fast duple time.

clue.text: Inveigle girl into clubs with alcoholic drink

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: the girl's name goes into the clubs-and-drink pairing

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink
Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes a girl into a club with drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle and to cajole both mean to coax or wheedle someone into something.

clue.text: French cleric's notes

parts.note: A is a musical note
B is a musical note
B again, a musical note
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Jottings from a priest in France.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French title for a priest or abbot.

clue.text: Fragrant rose our Fido destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed letters are broken up and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: The dog has trampled the sweet-smelling roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Odoriferous means giving off a smell, here a pleasant scent.

clue.text: English coin once securing new honour

indicators.note: the English coin holds the letter for new inside it

parts.note: the noble was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: An old English coin buys a fresh title.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise to the nobility, to honour with a title.

clue.text: Like abnormal narrowing damaging to insect

indicators.note: damaging the letters knocks them out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Something harmful to a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Stenotic describes stenosis, a medical narrowing of a passage such as a blood vessel.

clue.text: Lancelot's talent for getting in better sort of ale

parts.note: to better is to cap, outdo
a talent is an ability
brown ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A man named Lancelot has a knack for buying superior beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot Brown, the 18th-century English landscape gardener, was nicknamed 'Capability' for telling clients their grounds had capability for improvement. 'better' is a verb here: to cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot was the given name of the landscape gardener known by this nickname and surname.

clue.text: Taking care of supposedly humble types in the colonies?

definitions.text: Taking care of supposedly humble types in the colonies?

parts.words: Taking care of supposedly humble types in the colonies?
parts.note: the humble-bee is an old name for the bumblebee, so the humble types are bees and the colonies are their hives, not overseas territories

explanation.surface: Looking after lowly settlers in imperial outposts.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiculture means tending colonies of bees in hives.

clue.text: Woman's point I've accepted, avoiding the issue

indicators.note: the woman and the headland take in the contraction

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name, with its possessive S
a ness is a headland or point
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A woman's argument is conceded, though it dodged the question.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasiveness is the habit of dodging questions or the point at issue.

clue.text: Member shortening West Indian dance

indicators.note: the dance's name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the limbo is a dance from the West Indies

explanation.surface: A club member is curtailing a Caribbean dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body.

clue.text: Upset, like Samson when deprived of his strength?

definitions.text: like Samson when deprived of his strength?
definitions.meaning: Samson lost his strength when his hair was cut, so he was de-tressed, stripped of his tresses

explanation.surface: Samson was upset when he lost his power.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Delilah had Samson's hair cut, robbing him of his strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means upset or anxious, and punningly 'dis-tressed' means without hair.

clue.text: Time to move clumsily, serving tripe

parts.note: to waddle is to walk clumsily, like a duck

explanation.surface: It's time for a waiter to shuffle over with a plate of tripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is slang for nonsense, the same as twaddle.

clue.text: For which, permanently, european priest upset humanist

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the priest's title upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Rev is the short form of Reverend, a priest
Sir Thomas More was a Renaissance humanist

explanation.surface: A European cleric permanently offends a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says that 'for' plus the answer means permanently, as in 'for evermore'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'for evermore' means for all time, forever.

clue.text: Vessel I used in two rivers flow- ing into a third

indicators.note: the two rivers with I are set inside the third river's name, as tributaries flow into it

parts.note: the Teme is a river of the Welsh border and the English West Midlands

indicators.note: the letter I is placed in between the two rivers

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river, twice

explanation.surface: A boat travels through two rivers that join a third.
explanation.walkthrough: The Teme is a river flowing through Shropshire and Worcestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars, a sea vessel.

clue.text: Well-groomed board going round old quarters

indicators.note: the board's synonym goes round the letter for old

parts.note: a signboard is a sign
E (east) is a compass quarter, here taken twice

explanation.surface: A tidy company board travels around ancient districts.
explanation.definitionFit: Soignée is a borrowing from French for a woman elegantly turned out and carefully groomed.

clue.text: Possibly Munro's crowning feature

parts.note: a Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet; its crowning feature in winter is the white covering on its summit

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man named Munro's best attribute, such as his head of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Munro reads like a surname, but a Munro is a Scottish peak above 3,000 feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of snow covering a mountain top is called this.

clue.text: Ignore warrant officer, jolly pernicious type

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A soldier snubs a warrant officer, a cheerful but harmful character.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutworm is a moth caterpillar that destroys crops by cutting plants at the stem, so a harmful pest.

clue.text: Tone-modifying device given place inside bagpipe

indicators.note: the word for place goes inside the device

parts.note: a mute softens or alters an instrument's tone
to place is to set

explanation.surface: A tone-changing gadget is fitted into some bagpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A musette is a small French bagpipe.

clue.text: Finished port duke abandoned

indicators.note: the duke leaves the port's name, so his letter is dropped

parts.note: Dover is a Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: It's all over: the duke has left the harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means ended or finished, as in 'the game is over'.

clue.text: Literary assistant in USA names novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: In America, a book credits the writer's helpers.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a secretary who takes dictation or copies manuscripts for an author.

clue.text: Like a twang no Scottish girl produces

parts.note: na is Scots for no
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: A Scottish lass gives no twang in her speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal tone of voice, spoken through the nose.

clue.text: Autocrat turning head of celebrity

indicators.note: the first two letters of the celebrity word are turned round

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A dictator turns the head of a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the absolute ruler of Russia, an autocrat.

clue.text: Like reluctant batsmen and some clothes?

definitions.meaning: batsmen unwilling to be out refuse to leave the crease, the marked line where they stand in cricket
garments treated so they do not wrinkle

explanation.surface: Cricketers unwilling to leave and garments that keep their shape.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the marked line where the batsman stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that does not wrinkle easily is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Fuss? Nothing caused much around 1598

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's 'Much ... About Nothing' dates from about 1598, so nothing caused much of this

explanation.surface: A fuss about nothing in Shakespeare's day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Old transport system producing the dough!

parts.note: past means old, bygone
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A former railway network generating money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is a dough of flour, fat and water, rolled out for pies.

clue.text: Joyful PM loses weight, getting honour for it

indicators.note: the statesman sheds the weight from inside his name
the honour is received by the statesman in its place
the honour stands in for the lost weight, taking its position

parts.note: William Gladstone was a Victorian British Prime Minister
a ton is a unit of weight
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister sheds pounds and is rewarded with a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: In GLADSTONE, the TON is swapped for OM, leaving GLADS-OM-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladsome is an old-fashioned word for cheerful or glad.
